Re: Appeal of prior authorization denial  
Member: Emerson Delgado  
Member ID: W727121486  
Plan: Regence BlueShield Commercial/ACA  
Requested service: Lumbar fusion  
CPT: 22612  
Denial reference: POC-A93FE7E3B5-95850  
Date of denial notice: August 7, 2026

Dear Regence Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for lumbar fusion, CPT 22612. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The records summarized below address the applicable medical-necessity factors in Regence’s publicly available lumbar-fusion policy.

The policy states: “Clinical documentation to support criteria is required.” The submitted clinical information documents the following:

1. Neurogenic claudication and radicular symptoms  
I have experienced 14 months of progressive lower-back and leg pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness require me to stop. The symptoms improve with sitting. Examination documents neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes.

The policy identifies neurogenic claudication or radicular pain as a criterion for lumbar fusion in the setting of spinal stenosis.

2. Imaging-confirmed stenosis and instability  
The May 29, 2026 lumbar MRI and flexion-extension radiographs document severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina and grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension. These findings correspond to the documented leg symptoms and demonstrate instability at the level proposed for fusion.

The policy requires documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis on advanced imaging consistent with the individual’s symptoms, together with spondylolisthesis at a level to be fused or a high likelihood of postoperative instability.

3. Significant functional impairment  
The inability to stand or walk for more than 10 minutes because of leg pain and heaviness represents substantial functional impairment. This limitation is supported by the documented neurogenic claudication and sensory loss.

The policy allows functional impairment to be documented clinically or measured with the Oswestry Disability Index.

4. Failed conservative treatment  
The symptoms have persisted and progressed for 14 months despite conservative treatment, including:

- Supervised physical therapy focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, consisting of 16 visits over 10 weeks from May 7 through July 16, 2026, documented in the physical-therapy discharge note;
- NSAID treatment for four months with inadequate relief; and
- A corticosteroid injection on May 18, 2026, producing only four weeks of partial relief.

The policy requires documentation that at least three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the current symptoms. It further identifies physical therapy or a professionally directed home-exercise program and attempted treatment modalities such as prescription anti-inflammatory medication and injection therapy. The records document each of those treatment categories.

5. Nicotine status and other relevant clinical information  
I am a non-smoker. There is no active infection or untreated substance use, and BMI is 29. The policy requires that the individual be nicotine-free or have documented nicotine abstinence for at least six weeks before the planned procedure. My non-smoker status addresses this requirement; please advise if Regence requires an attestation or laboratory result.

The policy states that lumbar spinal fusion “may be considered medically necessary” for spinal stenosis when the specified criteria are met. Based on the documented neurogenic claudication, severe imaging-confirmed stenosis, L4-L5 spondylolisthesis with dynamic translation, substantial functional impairment, failed conservative treatment, and non-smoker status, the submitted records support medical necessity under the spinal-stenosis pathway.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22612. If Regence continues to find the documentation incomplete, please identify each specific missing document or criterion and provide the complete clinical-review criteria actually applied to this request. Please also consider the attached records, including the physical-therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, MRI and flexion-extension radiology reports, examination findings, and the surgeon’s supporting documentation.

This appeal must be received by February 3, 2027. Please send the appeal determination and any request for additional information in writing.

Sincerely,

Emerson Delgado
